SQL:
SELECT
  customers__regions.name AS "orders.customers.regions.name",
  DATE_TRUNC('MONTH', orders.order_date) AS "orders.order_date",
  CAST(SUM(orders.amount) AS DOUBLE) AS "orders.rev"
FROM orders AS orders
LEFT JOIN customers AS customers
  ON orders.customer_id = customers.id
LEFT JOIN regions AS customers__regions
  ON customers.region_id = customers__regions.id
WHERE
  (
    orders.order_date >= CAST('2025-01-01' AS DATE)
    AND orders.order_date < CAST('2025-04-01' AS DATE)
  )
GROUP BY
  customers__regions.name,
  DATE_TRUNC('MONTH', orders.order_date)
ORDER BY
  "orders.order_date" ASC,
  "orders.customers.regions.name" ASC

args.message: This is the saved monthly_rev query (sum of order amount by month) broken down by customer region for January to March 2025. Orders are linked to regions through their customer, and orders with no matching customer or region are kept rather than dropped. No such group shows up because every order in Q1 2025 has a known region (East, North, South or West). The regional figures add up exactly to the monthly totals: 10,070.12 for January, 8,920.94 for February and 9,816.20 for March. The Arctic region had no Q1 2025 orders.
